title: RinkRat Fairness Report
subtitle: Six-game opportunity, scoring roles, and matchup balance
evidenceStatus: Historical baseline and Production Scoring V4 sensitivity model
summary: RinkRat gives every active roster slot six scheduled NHL team games. The format reduces schedule-opportunity differences without removing drafting skill, roster decisions, injuries, hot streaks, or upset potential.

equalizes: The number of scheduled NHL team games assigned to each active roster slot.
The boundary between one scoring window and the next: game seven starts the next window.
The opportunity unit used by forwards, defensemen, and team goalie units.
doesNotEqualize: Player talent, role, shooting efficiency, or team quality.
Injuries, scratches, suspensions, missed appearances, or postponed games.
Draft quality, waiver decisions, roster timing, or matchup luck.
The calendar date on which different roster slots finish their independent windows.

methodology.windowRule: Games 1-6 form one roster-slot window; game 7 begins the next window. Calendar weeks were not used.
limitations: The historical baseline uses five complete 2013-18 regular seasons rather than the modern NHL scoring environment.
Historical primary and secondary assists were reconstructed with RinkRat's deterministic calibration fallback because exact sequencing was unavailable.
Player-level game-winning and overtime-goal bonuses were unavailable in the historical skater dataset and were omitted from that reconstruction.
Production Scoring V4 goalie distributions and matchup effects are sensitivity-model estimates, not future-season guarantees.
The complete modern-season exact-data replication remains an open acceptance gate before V4 is considered permanently calibrated.

positionProfiles.label: Center
positionProfiles.role: Offensive ceiling with a deeper replacement pool.

positionProfiles.label: Left Wing
positionProfiles.role: Boom-or-bust scoring with strong elite scarcity.

positionProfiles.label: Right Wing
positionProfiles.role: Similar starter-level scoring to LW with position-specific scarcity.

positionProfiles.label: Defense
positionProfiles.role: A steadier floor built from usage and multiple categories.

positionProfiles.label: Team Goalie Unit
positionProfiles.role: Highest typical total, stronger floor, and meaningful quality separation.

leagueSimulation.interpretation: A strong draft materially improves season results, while one six-game matchup still gives an underdog a realistic path to win.

archetypeChecks.label: Hit-only forward
archetypeChecks.finding: Hit-heavy grinders did not become elite forward options in the historical sample.

archetypeChecks.label: Shot volume without production
archetypeChecks.finding: High-shot, low-conversion players gained useful value but did not routinely overtake elite scorers.

archetypeChecks.label: High-TOI, low-offense defense
archetypeChecks.finding: Usage created a dependable floor, but no identified low-offense archetype became a top-12 defenseman solely through time on ice.

archetypeChecks.label: High-volume, poor-efficiency goalie unit
archetypeChecks.finding: Poor efficiency remained meaningfully weaker than strong goaltending with similar or lower volume.

archetypeChecks.label: Goalie draft wave
archetypeChecks.finding: Scoring V4 increases goalie separation, but the separate Projection V11 Draft slot curve still requires live V4 evidence and recalibration.

archetypeChecks.label: Modern-season replication
archetypeChecks.finding: The complete audit must be repeated with recent exact NHL data before the baseline is considered permanent.

acceptanceRanges.label: Matchups separated by at least 150 points
Top projected roster finishing top four
Maximum share of one position in repeated first rounds

protectedInvariants: Exactly six scheduled NHL team games per active roster-slot window.
The seventh NHL team game begins the next roster-slot window.
Window projections remain frozen once the window starts.
Queued roster moves activate at the intended boundary.
Different roster slots may have different active Matchup numbers.
The same NHL game cannot score twice for the same roster-slot window.
